description: The Observatory of Nature-based Solutions in Spain is an online knowledge platform that gathers Spanish nature-based solution projects, key organisations, documents and tools so that experiences can be found and replicated across cities and regions. It covers projects nationwide, including coastal adaptation case studies, a directory of research and innovation projects, a directory of professionals and publications; examples highlighted at launch include the La Marjal floodable park in Alicante (2015), hybrid dunes on Barcelona's metropolitan beaches (2014) and the renaturalisation of the Manzanares river in Madrid (2016). It was launched by Fundación Conama with the IUCN Centre for Mediterranean Cooperation in November 2020, with submissions filtered against criteria before they are added. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): all rights reserved (Fundación CONAMA grants no licence on its site content). Access is free of charge. Caveats: it is a curated web directory in Spanish, not a structured dataset. It is useful for finding Spanish green-blue infrastructure cases, such as floodable parks and dune restoration, for climate adaptation and flood risk studies; a related record is the Urban Nature Atlas.
